transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?

Hello, Dr. Smith. Well, I'm here because of a problem I'm having with bridges. 

It's gotten to the point where, the moment crossing one becomes unavoidable, I get this terrible rush of fear. It hits me before I’m even on the bridge itself. My heart just starts pounding in my chest, and my hands get all damp on the steering wheel—or on the armrest, if someone else is driving. It's just a very intense, immediate reaction, and I don't know how to handle it anymore.
Do you experience this same intense fear in other situations besides bridges—like being in high places, tunnels, or other specific settings—or is it really just bridges that trigger this reaction?

No, it's really just the bridges. Tunnels are fine, flying is fine, tall buildings... none of that bothers me. I mean, I'm 87 years old, I've seen a lot of things and been a lot of places, but it's just this one specific thing. If there's a bridge, that's when it happens. Everything else is perfectly okay.
How long have you been experiencing this intense fear specifically related to bridges—weeks, months, or years?

It's been years. Well, about two years and five months now, to be exact. It all started after a friend of mine died. There was an accident near a bridge route, and... well, this whole thing has just been going on ever since that happened.
Do you actively avoid crossing bridges or go out of your way to find alternate routes because of this fear, and has that avoidance caused problems in your daily life?

Yes, I absolutely avoid them. For over two years now, I've been planning all my errands and visits specifically to make sure I don't have to cross any bridges. It's really changed what I can do. I've had to give up taking trips to San Juan, and I can't go to my theater nights in Seattle anymore because of the routes. 

If there's a situation where I absolutely have to cross one, it's... it's a whole ordeal. I have to study the route beforehand, make sure the timing is just right, and I have to have someone else in the car with me. And even then, I just sit there frightened the entire way across. It's definitely caused a lot of problems for me.
